summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and a history of TIPS placement, was readmitted for coffee ground emesis and abdominal distension five days after a prior discharge for a similar episode. His hemoglobin was 8.1 g/dL, and he had a positive stool for blood. He underwent an EGD which showed esophagitis and portal hypertensive gastropathy without varices. He received one unit of packed red blood cells and was treated with pantoprazole, octreotide, and ceftriaxone, later transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin. A 6-liter therapeutic paracentesis was performed with albumin administration, and peritoneal fluid analysis showed no infection. His aspirin was held due to recurrent GI bleeding, and pravastatin was increased to 40 mg daily. He improved clinically, with resolution of symptoms and stable labs, and was discharged home with plans for close outpatient follow-up, continuation of liver-directed medications, and monitoring for transplant eligibility.
